knowledge.text: Synthetic maintenance dictionary; availability and all unreported timings are invented, not authentic operating procedures. vacuum_kpa is absolute condenser pressure in kPa: rising pressure means deteriorating vacuum, not a more negative gauge reading. cooling_flow_pct is percent of the assumed normal common-loop flow; no calibrated mass flow is known. Generator voltage_kv is machine-terminal line-to-line RMS voltage. Excitation may precede synchronization while breaker_closed=0 and active_power_mw=0. Residual terminal voltage can decay after disconnection; voltage alone proves neither grid connection nor restoration. Transformer voltage is the high-side indication; line, reactor and busbar voltages refer to their named terminals. available denotes ready/in service, not grid connection. Static CIM terminal state is not a live breaker contact. ts is acquisition time; available_at is delivery time. A stale channel retains one old held acquisition with delayed delivery, not repeated new measurements. Bad values exercise synthetic bounded corruption; missing values remain blank. Exclude non-good quality from physical decisions. Latched protection state and a new alarm edge differ. Unresolved active episodes are right-censored; an initial snapshot never invents a historical raise. UNIT_TRIP: Latched generator protection indication. An active edge asserts an observed indication, not its cause. A simulated reset may follow return by 10 seconds. BUSBAR_TRIP: Latched busbar protection indication. An active edge asserts an observed indication, not its cause. A simulated reset may follow return by 10 seconds. UNIT_TRIP_LATCHED: Initial snapshot of an already active generator protection latch. Timestamp is snapshot acquisition, never a new trip or historical raise time. Reset follows simulated return by 10 seconds when represented. BUSBAR_TRIP_LATCHED: Initial snapshot of an already active busbar protection latch. Timestamp is snapshot acquisition, never a new trip or historical raise time. Reset follows simulated return by 10 seconds when represented. RETURN_TO_SERVICE: Informational return indication episode: active on the simulated return, cleared by acknowledgement 5 seconds later. Does not clear a protection code or prove connected state without measurements. PLANNED_TEST_STATUS: Informational status-test episode: active 5 seconds before the completion clear. No equipment switching or new outage is asserted. TELEMETRY_REFRESH: Informational refresh episode: active 3 seconds before the acknowledgement clear. Existing delayed and future deliveries remain exclusion probes.
knowledge.title: Synthetic instrument and indication dictionary

knowledge.text: Synthetic maintenance dictionary; availability and all unreported timings are invented, not authentic operating procedures. vacuum_kpa is absolute condenser pressure in kPa: rising pressure means deteriorating vacuum, not a more negative gauge reading. cooling_flow_pct is percent of the assumed normal common-loop flow; no calibrated mass flow is known. Generator voltage_kv is machine-terminal line-to-line RMS voltage. Excitation may precede synchronization while breaker_closed=0 and active_power_mw=0. Residual terminal voltage can decay after disconnection; voltage alone proves neither grid connection nor restoration. Transformer voltage is the high-side indication; line, reactor and busbar voltages refer to their named terminals. available denotes ready/in service, not grid connection. Static CIM terminal state is not a live breaker contact. ts is acquisition time; available_at is delivery time. A stale channel retains one old held acquisition with delayed delivery, not repeated new measurements. Bad values exercise synthetic bounded corruption; missing values remain blank. Exclude non-good quality from physical decisions. Latched protection state and a new alarm edge differ. Unresolved active episodes are right-censored; an initial snapshot never invents a historical raise. UNIT_TRIP: Latched generator protection indication. An active edge asserts an observed indication, not its cause. A simulated reset may follow return by 10 seconds. BUSBAR_TRIP: Latched busbar protection indication. An active edge asserts an observed indication, not its cause. A simulated reset may follow return by 10 seconds. UNIT_TRIP_LATCHED: Initial snapshot of an already active generator protection latch. Timestamp is snapshot acquisition, never a new trip or historical raise time. Reset follows simulated return by 10 seconds when represented. BUSBAR_TRIP_LATCHED: Initial snapshot of an already active busbar protection latch. Timestamp is snapshot acquisition, never a new trip or historical raise time. Reset follows simulated return by 10 seconds when represented. RETURN_TO_SERVICE: Informational return indication episode: active on the simulated return, cleared by acknowledgement 5 seconds later. Does not clear a protection code or prove connected state without measurements. PLANNED_TEST_STATUS: Informational status-test episode: active 5 seconds before the completion clear. No equipment switching or new outage is asserted. TELEMETRY_REFRESH: Informational refresh episode: active 3 seconds before the acknowledgement clear. Existing delayed and future deliveries remain exclusion probes.
knowledge.title: Synthetic instrument and indication dictionary

knowledge.text: Fixture policy only. Given a simulated busbar notification, verify fresh de-energized state and available protection indications without requiring the original transition. Review work permits and protection boundaries without assigning a cause. Consult line limit advice and recommend authorized temporary EMS rating changes, then notify the operator. Existing generator or reactor outages are context, not a new loss. Given a restoration notification, verify current energized state and applicable return/protection indications before recommending removal of temporary overrides under authorization; never operate physical switchgear.

knowledge.text: Fixture permits and timestamps are invented. Stable out-of-service indications and planned test/status alarms do not establish a new contingency. Confirm fresh data, permit scope and topology. Treat missing/bad/stale signals as an evidence gap, not normality. Scheduled protection maintenance on 5B1 does not by itself establish the cause of a protection operation elsewhere.
